text: Chapter 1 introduced exact pinning as a defense against silent breaks. This lesson treats pinning specifically as a reproducibility requirement: if you can't reinstall the exact environment that produced a result, a git tag only gets you half the way to reproducing it.

This lesson covers why pinning is a reproducibility concern and not just a stability concern, how to snapshot an entire resolved environment rather than just top-level packages, tying a pinned environment to a specific experiment tag, and what to do when a result was produced under a dependency version you can no longer install.

A pyproject.toml with an exact pin is necessary but not sufficient — it pins the direct dependency, not that package's own internal dependencies, which can still resolve differently across machines or time without a full lockfile. Generate and commit a full lockfile capturing the entire resolved dependency tree, and name the frozen snapshot after the experiment tag, making the connection between this result and this exact environment explicit and searchable instead of implicit and easy to lose.

Extend the tagging practice from last lesson: commit the lockfile alongside the tagged commit, so retrieving the tag also retrieves the exact environment. Now a single git show command against that tag retrieves the exact dependency tree active when the result was produced, with no separate record-keeping required outside git itself.

Over enough time, a pinned version may become genuinely uninstallable — a package index removes an old release, or it's incompatible with a newer Python version you're forced onto. When this happens, document explicitly that exact reproduction is no longer possible, rather than silently re-running on a different version and reporting the same old number as if nothing changed. Re-run the experiment under the closest currently-installable version, and report the new result as a new, separately tagged experiment — not a patch to the old one. If the discrepancy matters, that discrepancy is itself worth investigating, since it may reveal a silent break.

Next lesson pins down the last remaining piece: the specific run-time parameters — random seed, shot count, backend version — without which 'reproduce this result' is still underspecified even with the code and the environment both solved.
